files.purpose: The shared design-token namespace and base component kit of the app's chrome: `enum Chrome` holds every window, sticky-row, sidebar and card metric, the colour accessors that forward to ThemeManager.spec, and the hover/panelSlide/settleFlight animations, and the rest of the file builds the reusable controls on those tokens (glass capsules and circles, icon/menu/text buttons that open PopoverMenu popovers, sidebar rows and search fields, the pane-top veil and compact title driven by ChromeScrollModel, settings cards/sections/rows). It also owns the window's backdrop (Liquid Glass or solid fill, optional wallpaper, scrim, tint and 1pt hairline), the softAppear and settleGlide transitions, and the two AppKit NSView bridges that either start a window drag (WindowDragArea) or refuse one under chrome controls (NoWindowDragArea). In 1.6.2 it moves most fixed point sizes to Dynamic Type text styles, redefines secondaryText as primary at 70%, and adds ChromeQuietButtonStyle and the animatable ChromeRevealLayout.

feature_notes: ChromeScrollModel.update(travel:): raw = (travel - 10) / (44 - 10); clamped to 0...1; quantized = round(clamped / 0.04) * 0.04; progress is assigned only when the quantized value differs, so the veil and compact title re-render at most 26 distinct steps.
Chrome.contentTopInset = chromeTopPadding 12 + capsuleHeight 32 + contentBreathBelowChrome 28 = 72, equal to veilHeight 72.
Chrome.accent falls back to NSColor.controlAccentColor when the theme spec has no accent (System/Light/Dark per the comment); the doc comment says the window root also applies it as the view tint.

WindowBackdrop at the solid end (opacity >= 0.98) draws a plain fill instead of glass to avoid a full-window glass sample every frame; with a wallpaper the scrim is not drawn at all and the wallpaper's own opacity equals the transparency setting.
ChromeGlassSurface draws a flat fill instead of glass whenever isOnGlassPanel is true, to avoid glass-on-glass double sampling.
chromeGlassFieldCapsule exists because an interactive glass press bounce flickered as the field took focus; it is the non-interactive variant.

NoWindowDragArea sits in the background of these controls only: ChromeCapsule (320), ChromeIconButton (381), ChromeMenuButton (408), ChromeCircleButton (435), ChromeCircleMenu (468), ChromeTextMenu (512), ChromeTextButton (552), ChromeSearchField (867), GlassPickerButton (930), ChromeSegmentedPicker.swift:42 and ChromeVisualPicker.swift:48. SidebarRow (710-739), SidebarSearchField (784-816) and Popovers.swift RowActionsButton (389-400) have none. The doc comment (1104-1113) says empty chrome around the controls still drags the window like a title bar. WindowDragArea does the opposite for designated drag stretches; both WindowDragView (1095) and NoWindowDragView (1123) override acceptsFirstMouse(for:) to return true.
SidebarSearchField: up/down arrow handling only claims the key when onMove is non-nil; the doc says onMove is declared last so a bare trailing closure still binds to onSubmit.
ChromeSearchField keeps its clear button laid out even when empty (opacity 0, disabled, accessibility hidden) so the text never shifts.

ChromeRevealLayout (286-304) sizes its single child with ProposedViewSize(width: proposal.width, height: nil) and reports CGSize(width: natural.width, height: natural.height * min(max(fraction, 0), 1)); placeSubviews always places the child at bounds.origin, anchor .topLeading, with ProposedViewSize(width: bounds.width, height: nil), i.e. at full natural height even when the slot is shorter (the placement width is bounds.width, not natural.width); it returns .zero with no child. The layout itself does NOT clip: at fraction 0 the child overflows its zero-height slot. The doc comment (282-285) speaks of 'the clip', but the clip is added by callers, e.g. ModelsSettingsPage.swift 379, 393 and 429 `.clipped()` after ChromeRevealLayout. A port must clip at each call site or build the clip into its layout.
ChromeQuietButtonStyle renders configuration.label unchanged: no pressed feedback while keeping Button semantics.
PaneTopVeil was formerly Liquid Glass under a gradient mask; the comment says it is now two gradient fills to avoid a backdrop sample and offscreen mask per frame.

Needs a decision rather than a source read.

files.purpose: A compact settings-row control that lays every option out as a small capsule button inside one glass capsule strip, with the chosen one filled in the accent colour. It is for options that are a few short words or numbers; each option may show an SF Symbol instead of its title while the title stays the accessibility label.

files.purpose: A settings-row control of two or three same-size tiles, each showing one caller-supplied symbol on a stage with the option's name captioned underneath, modelled on macOS Appearance's Light / Dark / Auto chooser. The chosen tile wears a 2pt accent ring and its symbol takes the accent colour; ChromeVisualTileMetrics fixes the tile measures so pickers of two and three options align.

files.purpose: An "info.circle" mark that opens a caller-supplied explainer popover as soon as the pointer hovers it, keeps the popover open while the pointer is over either the mark or the popover, and closes it 320 ms after the pointer has left both. A click toggles the popover too, and the mark is not keyboard-focusable.

files.purpose: The app's native-popover menu system that replaces pull-down menus: PopoverMenu is the scrolling body every chrome and composer button opens, PopoverItem is the row (checkmark column, icon, styled title, detail, destructive tint and an in-place confirmation such as "Copied"), with section headers, notes and dividers. It also carries the plumbing for AppKit-hosted popovers (NSPopover.setFixedContent, a pre-measuring PopoverScroll, and a boxed closePopover environment value) and the RowAction model that feeds both a sidebar row's ellipsis popover and its context menu.

feature_notes: setFixedContent exists because an NSHostingController publishes preferredContentSize after show(relativeTo:), and AppKit then resizes the shown panel from its top edge, leaving the arrow floating above the anchor; sizingOptions = [] leaves contentSize in charge.

PopoverScroll with a width is 'premeasured': later onGeometryChange heights are ignored (the panel never resizes), so the scroll absorbs any difference; without a width, contentHeight follows onGeometryChange.
PopoverCloseBox compares by reference so the environment value does not invalidate every reader on each update; closePopover is the plain-closure facade that wraps a new box on set.
RowAction.id is its title, so two actions with the same title in one list collide in ForEach.
Checkmark column is kept for every row of a choice list whenever isChecked is non-nil (true or false).

files.purpose: Draws a project's mark (an emoji or a filled SF Symbol, defaulting to "folder.fill") and provides the 300x420 popover picker that chooses it: a "Search symbols" field, an Emoji grid of 131 fixed emoji, a Popular section of 56 shortlisted filled symbols filtered against the system catalogue, then every group of the generated ProjectSymbolCatalogue, and a Folder tile that clears the mark. Core owns the ProjectIcon value; this file only renders and edits it through a binding.

matchingSymbols (115-123): needle = query.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces) (spaces and tabs only, not newlines); empty -> []; else every ProjectSymbolCatalogue.all name that localizedCaseInsensitiveContains the needle, with filledForm(of: needle) inserted at index 0 when it is non-nil and not already present. Emoji are never searched. When a non-empty query matches nothing, matchingSymbols is empty and body (144-148) falls back to the full default view (Emoji grid plus every group); there is no 'no results' state.

filledForm(of:) (128-134): if the name ends in ".fill" or ".inverse" return it only if NSImage(systemSymbolName:accessibilityDescription:) knows it; else return name + ".fill" if NSImage knows that; else nil. The typed text is not lowercased first. The doc comments (113-114 'when the catalogue knows that name', 126 'its .fill mark when the catalogue has one') say catalogue, but the check is against the system symbol set, not ProjectSymbolCatalogue.all, so a search can offer a symbol absent from the generated catalogue. On Windows this check must become a lookup in the substitute glyph set.
Selection is shown by symbolName equality for symbols and emoji equality for emoji; the Folder tile is selected when icon is nil.
Emoji identity in ForEach is the emoji string (id: \.self).
